references.text: Refers to Esau marrying Hittite women, which was a source of grief for Isaac and Rebekah.
Rebekah expresses her displeasure with Esau's Hittite wives and does not want Jacob to marry a woman from Canaan.
Isaac sends Jacob to Paddan-Aram to find a wife among his relatives, in line with his and Rebekah's wish to avoid marriage with Canaanite women.
Both verses document Esau's reaction to Jacob receiving the blessing and birthright, and together they form a complete account of the origin of the conflict.
The verses belong to the same event; 28:6 refers to the blessing given after Isaac was deceived in 27:21.
Hebrews 11:20 provides the theological interpretation of the event described in Genesis 28:6, confirming that Isaac's blessing was driven by faith.
The verses mark the beginning and end points of Jacob's time in Paddan-Aram, showing the connection between the mission he received and God's blessing upon his return.
